rv.q: “Six,” the first new musical of the 2021-2022 season, spreads exactly the kind of energizing, inspirational illumination this town aches for.
Six is irresistible from start to finish.
The songs here, by Toby Marlow and Lucy Moss, are all whip-smart and catchy.
The musical is a clever, catchy and supremely entertaining 80-minute celebration of female empowerment that gives voice to the six wives of Henry VIII.
It's not a treatise but a lark and a provocation — and a work of blatantly commercial theater.

“Six” is a practical, entertaining, well-executed, self-aware show that knows how to please its audience and delivers a soupçon of Broadway pizzazz and good humor without asking a lot or overstaying its welcome.
More musicals could learn this lesson: skip the feints at naturalism and just get down to the songs.
For those looking for pure diversion, with bits of sung history tossed in, “Six” will be an unalloyed pleasure.
The queens sing their heads off and the audience loses its mind.
This is definitely a history of the English monarchy for people who found the Dynasty -style salaciousness of The Tudors too highbrow, and your enjoyment may depend on how far puberty is behind you.
Broadway gets to experience this rockin’ rewrite of 16th-century her-story.
An audience show for a wide audience, Six is a rafter-raising entertainment that’ll get you throwing your proverbial bonnet in the air (but please keep that mask on, for now).
Six truly is the top ticket to celebrate the return of the live stage show.

The songs are, without hyperbole, miracles of modern musical theatre: completely, line-by-line relevant to what is happening onstage while maintaining a universal pop appeal that can play without context.
You'll laugh. You'll cry. You'll dance. It's everything a theatre experience should be and more.

It is one of the cleverest, wittiest, flashiest musicals in town—and sets up home in New York after rave reviews wherever it has played, including the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, where it began life in 2017, and London’s West End.
It's a glittering pop confection with enough teeth and muscle to turn a mnemonic device of history into an attention-worthy piece of herstory.
SIX was one of the tragedies of the pandemic, set to open on the night Broadway went dark back in March 2020.
As spectacle, it's highly conceived kitsch.
It was a similar phenomenon to Be More Chill, another show made famous by fan sharing — except that Six has actual wit and substance.
But the electricity winds up feeling static.
Are young women finally tired of being pandered to by Broadway musicals?
Notwithstanding the dynamic score, 'Six' is weighed down by a labored book, bargain-basement scenic design, and clunky dance choreography.
The major problem with this about-face declaration is that everything said or sung before it doesn’t feel changed, making it come off as either a huge structural misstep or completely insincere.
Marlow and Moss skillfully combine pop references with nods to musical genres popular five hundred years ago, making the show the most entertaining history lesson on stage.
The Six strutt forward with queen-like assuredness, demanding to be taken seriously to the sound of whimsical harpsichord remixes and a driving pop score.
They have created a generous, funny, provocative show that races by you, grabs your hand and flies up into the stratosphere.
I can happily note this smart, silly production remains just as easy to embrace.

The queens are still reigning on Broadway, where each of Henry’s lovers conveys their unfortunate tales of woe through song in 80 minutes of pop bliss that doubles both as entertainment and a history lesson.
It was a phenomenal concert, but not really a play.

cn.t: Critics celebrate SIX as an exuberant, high-energy pop concert musical that reclaims Henry VIII's wives' stories with infectious girl-power anthems, dazzling performances, and joyous feminist spirit—a supercharged Broadway triumph.

vs.sum: The Lena Horne Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, with clear views even from the rear mezzanine. The sound quality is well-balanced across the theater. However, the seating is quite tight, especially for taller patrons, which affects comfort. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic architecture and restored interior, providing a charming atmosphere.

I love Six... it's a good show and it's going to be a good time.
